label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy calls the Lion a coward.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

unit: Dorothy and her companions leave the Emerald City and travel west to find the Wicked Witch. The Witch spots them from her castle and sends wolves, crows, bees, and Winkie soldiers to destroy them, but Dorothy's friends defeat each wave. Finally, the Witch uses the Golden Cap to summon the Winged Monkeys, who destroy the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, capture the Lion, and carry Dorothy and Toto to the Witch's castle, where Dorothy is made a servant while secretly helping the imprisoned Lion.

label: History
value: Seeking to return to Kansas, the Wizard eventually constructed a new hot-air balloon alongside Dorothy.
unit: Originally from Omaha, the Wizard once worked in a circus before arriving in the land of Oz floating in a runaway hot-air balloon. Upon descending from the clouds, local residents mistook him for a great wizard; he then usurped the throne from King Pastoria, ordered the construction of the Emerald City, and hid the infant Princess Ozma away with Mombi, whom he taught magic tricks. While ruling, he encountered the Winged Monkeys in the Land of the West, an experience he had no desire to repeat. Seeking to return to Kansas, he eventually constructed a new hot-air balloon alongside Dorothy, but when its ropes snapped as Dorothy chased her dog Toto, the balloon carried him away alone, leaving her behind.

They thought the Great Wizard would send for them at once, but he did not. They had no word from him the next day, nor the next, nor the next. The waiting was tiresome and wearing, and at last they grew vexed that Oz should treat them in so poor a fashion, after sending them to undergo hardships and slavery. So the Scarecrow at last asked the green girl to take another message to Oz, saying if he did not let them in to see him at once they would call the Winged Monkeys to help them, and find out whether he kept his promises or not. When the Wizard was given this message he was so frightened that he sent word for them to come to the Throne Room at four minutes after nine o’clock the next morning. He had once met the Winged Monkeys in the Land of the West, and he did not wish to meet them again.

unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

label: History
value: Mombi was taught magical tricks by the Wizard of Oz
unit: Mombi was an old sorceress living in the Gillikin region of Oz who was taught magical tricks by the Wizard of Oz and obtained the Powder of Life from Nikidik. After returning home with new magic items, she used the powder to bring Tip's wooden creation, Jack Pumpkinhead, to life, but her plan to turn Tip into a marble statue caused the boy to steal her remaining powder and flee. She later aligned with General Jinjur to stop the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, conjuring magical illusions and confusing fields to impede their travel. When Glinda surrounded the Emerald City, Mombi attempted to evade capture through disguises and shape-shifting—including transforming into a rose, an ant, and a giant Griffin—before being pursued and caught in the desert. Under questioning with Glinda's truth-detecting pearl, Mombi confessed to having transformed the baby Princess Ozma into Tip, and she subsequently performed the incantation to break the spell and restore the princess to her true form.

passages.v02:c04:p0001: “Jack’s all right, and works fine!” he said to himself, panting with the unusual exertion. But just then he discovered the man’s left arm had fallen off in the journey so he went back to find it, and afterward, by whittling a new and stouter pin for the shoulder-joint, he repaired the injury so successfully that the arm was stronger than before. Tip also noticed that Jack’s pumpkin head had twisted around until it faced his back; but this was easily remedied. When, at last, the man was set up facing the turn in the path where old Mombi was to appear, he looked natural enough to be a fair imitation of a Gillikin farmer,—and unnatural enough to startle anyone that came on him unawares.
